title: The Charity Accounts
subtitle: Generosity, audited
briefing: A small children's charity discovers a shortfall of ninety thousand pounds during its annual audit. The money left the account in forty-one payments to a supplier that provided real services, at prices nobody questioned. The trustees are volunteers and the finance function is one part-time member of staff.
solution: Trevor Lisle, the part-time finance officer, created a second supplier record with a name one character different from a genuine one, and directed forty-one payments to it. The trustee whose signature appeared on the approvals had signed blank forms in good faith, and the volunteer coordinator's cash handling errors were sloppy but honest.

suspects.name: Trevor Lisle
suspects.motive: Sole control of the supplier list, the payment run and the reconciliation.

statements.question: Who approved the payments?
statements.text: Every one was approved by a trustee. The forms are on file.

statements.question: Are the supplier records sound?
statements.text: They are as they have always been. I did not create any of them.

statements.question: How is the bank reconciled?
statements.text: Monthly, by me, and reviewed by the treasurer.

suspects.name: Marion Deeks
suspects.motive: Her signature appears on all forty-one approval forms.

statements.question: Who approved the payments?
statements.text: I signed forms. I am ashamed to say some of them were blank when I signed them.

statements.question: Are the supplier records sound?
statements.text: I would not know one supplier from another.

statements.question: How is the bank reconciled?
statements.text: Trevor prepares it and I review it. I see a summary, not the detail.

suspects.name: Nita Shah
suspects.motive: Two cash reconciliations were out by small amounts.

statements.question: Who approved the payments?
statements.text: Nothing to do with me. I handle collection tins.

statements.question: Are the supplier records sound?
statements.text: I have never seen the supplier list.

statements.question: How is the bank reconciled?
statements.text: I reconcile the tins. Twice I have been out by a few pounds and I reported both.

suspects.name: Douglas Mure
suspects.motive: Waived the requirement for a second approver two years ago.

statements.question: Who approved the payments?
statements.text: A trustee, under the scheme of delegation. Which I now see was too loose.

statements.question: Are the supplier records sound?
statements.text: That is an operational matter. I have to be able to trust it.

statements.question: How is the bank reconciled?
statements.text: Monthly. The treasurer reviews it and reports to the board.

evidence.name: Payment pattern
evidence.description: Forty-one payments, each just below the second-approver threshold.

evidence.name: Personal destination account
evidence.description: The supplier payments went to a personal current account.

evidence.name: Genuine signatures
evidence.description: The trustee's signature on the approval forms is authentic.

evidence.name: Near-duplicate supplier
evidence.description: Two supplier records differ by a single character.

evidence.name: System audit trail
evidence.description: The duplicate supplier record was created from the finance officer's account.

evidence.name: Unreviewed reconciliation
evidence.description: The reconciliation is prepared and reviewed without independent checking.

evidence.name: Pre-signed blank forms
evidence.description: Six unused approval forms already carry the treasurer's signature.

evidence.name: Cash discrepancies
evidence.description: Two small cash discrepancies, both self-reported.

evidence.name: Matching bank details
evidence.description: The destination sort code matches the finance officer's payroll record.

evidence.name: Delegation waiver
evidence.description: The second-approver requirement was waived two years earlier.

evidence.name: Supplier correspondence
evidence.description: The genuine supplier has no record of the duplicated account.

timeline.text: A near-duplicate supplier record is created.
The first payment is made to the new supplier.
The annual audit identifies the shortfall.

hints: Compare the supplier list against itself, character by character.
A genuine signature does not mean a genuine approval.
Follow the money to an account, and the account to a person.
